correctness.rationale: The claimed finite graph is explicitly defined and has 30 edges. Complete exact enumeration finds 60 perfect matchings and 44,281 nonempty simplices, corroborated by a separate subset-DP matching count. A deterministic 22,113-pair discrete-Morse matching is verified acyclic by a topological sort over all 244,830 Hasse incidences. Its critical 0-,3-,4-cell counts are 1,42,12. Exact signed boundary elimination computes a 42-by-12 matrix with 64 entries of size one; eleven primitive unit pivots give integral diagonal I_11 and zero remainder. A separate Smith-normal-form computation confirms invariant factors 1 repeated eleven times. Since the three-skeleton is a wedge of 42 three-spheres, Hurewicz identifies its three-dimensional attaching classes with Z^42; the integral diagonalization realizes eleven trivial degree-one pairs and one null four-cell attachment, proving the stated wedge of 31 three-spheres and one four-sphere. The finite verifier and independently regenerated certificate replay successfully. No infinite-family or independent-validation claim is made.

value.rationale: The Desargues graph is the canonical nonplanar bipartite Levi graph of a classical ten-point/ten-line configuration. The homotopy classification is a natural exact topological invariant of perfect-matching extendibility, motivated by published questions about perfect-matching complexes of bipartite graphs. It differs fundamentally from the known ordinary Desargues matching-complex homotopy: the perfect-matchable faces exclude 68,910 matchings, and the result is a mixed-dimensional wedge of 31 three-spheres plus one four-sphere. The exact 400 minimal extension obstructions support the invariant’s structural mathematical content. The claim is intentionally one finite natural classification, not presented as a general theorem or a paper-sized breakthrough.
